title: Capture decision documents into Annals
summary: Classify completed root exchanges as decision or no-decision, render full normalized conversation into Markdown, and deliver through the sole active observer document path.
use_when: Post-activation decisions in completed local Codex root turns should be captured automatically.
Krisis observer coverage, pending Annals delivery, or a diagnosed failed observation should be inspected or recovered.
A missed Stop-hook correlation should be reconciled from normalized Conversations history.
do_not_use_when: Decision accounts should be searched or read after acceptance; use Annals.
A daily digest, candidate-review workflow, or supersession graph is wanted.
Raw transcripts, files, commands, tools, reasoning, or assistant-only proposals are intended as decision authority.
outcome: One durable exchange verdict and, for a positive result, a target-bound immutable document accepted idempotently by Annals.
effects: The Stop hook durably records only a turn correlation; reconciliation may independently enqueue missed eligible completed turns.
One serial worker saves a frozen conversation and exact Nucleus request/result, records coverage and a document outbox atomically, and delivers the oldest pending document before new classification.
After matching Annals acceptance, Krisis clears the outbox body and retains delivery identity and receipt. The private document run still retains source and classification for recovery.
authority: A decision is an attributable user transition from practical openness to an explicit settlement constraining intended future behavior or state.
The agent decides whether the selected exchange contains a user decision under its instructions. Code validates source integrity and result structure and renders all captured user/assistant text.
Krisis owns capture and delivery state, Nucleus owns execution evidence, Conversations owns normalized source resolution, and Annals owns the accepted library.
success: Each eligible completed exchange has one durable decision or no-decision outcome.
A positive result has a summary heading, full normalized conversation through the selected exchange, a stable document key, exact Markdown bytes and digest, and a durable target-bound outbox.

Before classification, Krisis verifies and binds the exact Annals config path and expected library ID; delivery succeeds only when that target returns a matching created or replayed acceptance receipt.
failure_and_recovery: The full frozen conversation must fit the prompt bound. Oversized sources fail without truncation; no context expansion or content-fitness check is imposed.
An ambiguous request or acknowledgement resumes the same frozen run and job; saved results remain valid after later runtime failure.
Annals outage leaves exact document bytes pending without reclassification. Source, target, digest, receipt, or dependency mismatch stops processing.
Terminal observation retry and proven-unavailable unbound source abandonment require their explicit guarded recovery commands.
privacy: Nucleus receives full normalized user/assistant conversation in a prompt bounded to 262144 UTF-8 bytes. Workspace, local execution and web access are disabled.
Private document runs retain full normalized conversation, request, and accepted classification. Routine logs contain bounded codes and opaque correlations.
Annals receives the complete rendered document. It requires no decision sections or Source metadata.
does_not_authorize: Deploying or changing live schedules, Annals libraries, Nucleus registrations, authentication, or existing state.
Using a source other than the cited user message to authorize a decision.
Reading or mutating either product's SQLite database directly, widening classifier scope, or restoring retired digest/review behavior.

consumers.statement: The local current user and installed Krisis observer may capture post-baseline decisions into one explicitly configured dedicated Annals decisions library.
This capability is not a decision browser, daily digest, review queue, result tracker, or general transcript exporter.

preconditions.statement: Observation requires the write-once activation baseline, a uniquely resolved eligible completed root turn, compatible Conversations and Nucleus contracts, and private migration-compatible Krisis state.
Delivery requires an absolute Annals executable, an absolute dedicated-library config, and the exact 32-lowercase-hex expected library ID.

inputs.statement: The source is the full normalized root conversation through one selected completed exchange. Later exchanges are excluded and required history is never truncated.
The classifier submits only is_decision and summary. A positive result requires a nonblank single-line summary; a negative result requires null.
File-change evidence, raw items, real source IDs, paths, commands, tools, reasoning, approvals, web, and local execution are not classifier inputs.

outputs.statement: Hook, activation, processing, status and receipt types remain operational interfaces. Status includes complete counts and bounded failures with failures_has_more; historical accounts_pending_annals and accounts_accepted_by_annals fields count document handoffs. Legacy lifecycle reads preserve old records.
Positive output is an ordinary Markdown document with the escaped summary heading and all captured user/assistant messages. Negative output has no document.

data_semantics.statement: Decision means a user settlement under the classifier instructions. No-decision is durable negative coverage for the selected completed exchange.
Context, action, and result record observations available at capture time; Unknown means no observation was captured for that field.
Annals created and replayed both mean the exact producer key and digest were accepted by the configured dedicated library.

identity_and_units.statement: The producer document key derives outside the model from a serialized host/thread/turn identity tuple hashed with SHA-256. The content digest hashes exact UTF-8 document bytes.
Exchange completion and observer timestamps use Unix seconds. Prompt and content digests use exact UTF-8 bytes; summary length counts Unicode scalar values.
Krisis publishes no pricing, usage, or accounting unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: A completed observation covers one eligible exchange and preserves the full normalized conversation prefix used to classify it.
A positive document remains pending until a matching Annals receipt commits. The outbox body is cleared only afterward.
No wall-clock bound from turn completion through classification or Annals acceptance is promised.

access.statement: Supported access is the local current-user krisis CLI, exact installed Stop hook, and release-pinned krisis/observer Clockwork runner; direct SQLite access is unsupported.
Cross-product calls use only the sealed Conversations, Nucleus protocol-v1, and Annals CLI interfaces with explicit configuration.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: The private run saves the source, exact request, job identity and accepted tool result before acknowledgement. After the job settles, coverage and exact document outbox commit in one SQLite transaction. Interruption resumes the same saved run.
Observation is serial; one pending Annals delivery is attempted before new classification, so an outage never causes reclassification or parallel ownership.

Annals acceptance clears only the pending outbox body; the private run remains available for recovery. Local document build/render commands use the same builder but do not enqueue or advance coverage. Retired paths cannot produce new accounts.

operational_limits.statement: The full encoded prompt is at most 262144 UTF-8 bytes; history is never truncated. A positive summary has at most 1000 Unicode scalar values. Annals files are at most 1 MiB.
One observation has one frozen full-history source per attempt. Ambiguous outcomes resume the same job. A new attempt requires explicit retry after a definitive terminal failure.
No throughput, queue-depth, storage-capacity, latency, or retention service-level objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Krisis schema 5 uses krisis/decision-document/1 with immutable submit-decision input/result schemas version 1 and Annals exchange 2. Migration refuses old pending account handoffs and in-flight observations/jobs until settled. Old codecs and receipts remain historical.
Legacy Decisions schema versions and classifier receipts remain decodable for migration and recovery, while digest and review commands and schedules remain disabled.
No future compatibility window, retention horizon, or release cadence is promised.

reliances.statement: Eligible turn discovery, exact normalized source resolution, message ordering, and timestamp precision rely on Conversations.
Bounded classification execution and durable tool transport rely on Nucleus without transferring decision or delivery authority.
Document acceptance and dedicated-library identity rely on Annals; Krisis retains delivery authority until a matching receipt commits.
Periodic observer invocation relies on Clockwork immutable definitions and the krisis/observer binding.
Immediate Stop-hook correlation relies on the local Codex hook facility, for which no installed Chancery contract is declared.
